subject.title: sec (7/9): redact only declared scanner secretEnv values

question: Should existing secret-looking names declared under `env` keep their current error-text redaction compatibility while `secretEnv` becomes the explicit always-redacted category?
rationale: The PR intentionally changes a credential-redaction boundary for already-valid user profiles, so maintainers must choose whether explicit configuration may silently replace the current name-based safety backstop.

options.title: Preserve legacy redaction
options.body: Redact declared `secretEnv` values and continue redacting secret-looking legacy `env` names, with regression tests for existing profile configurations.

options.title: Adopt a breaking explicit-only contract
options.body: Allow all `env` values to appear in failures only with an explicit upgrade notice and a maintainer-approved migration policy for existing scanner profiles.

options.title: Pause this series step
options.body: Defer the contract change until the project decides how artifact secrecy and configuration migrations should interact.

recommendation.title: Preserve legacy redaction
recommendation.body: Redact declared `secretEnv` values and continue redacting secret-looking legacy `env` names, with regression tests for existing profile configurations.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor introduced and recently maintained the user-defined scanner configuration and execution path affected by the compatibility decision.
